[中文版 →](getting-started-zh.html)

sleepcleanr detects and corrects typing errors in sleep-diary times and durations, and keeps a
record of every change. It is research software and is not on CRAN. This page takes you from
installation to a first run. Read [Input data and configuration](column-mapping.html) first if
your data are not yet in the expected shape.

## 1. Install

Install in a plain R session in which sleepcleanr is not loaded, from a directory that is not a
checkout of this repository (a checkout has its own `renv` library, which hides your system
packages).

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("cyracaid/sleepdiary-cleaner@v1.7.2", upgrade = "never", force = TRUE)
```

Then **restart R** and check what is loaded:

```r
library(sleepcleanr)
getNamespaceVersion("sleepcleanr")      # "1.7.2"
```

Reinstalling while the package is loaded in another R window can leave a corrupted installation
(`lazy-load database ... is corrupt`). Close every R session first, install, then restart.

## 2. Prepare a project folder

Make one folder per run. Put in it your data file and a config YAML (copy `inst/config_template.yaml`
and edit the `data` section). If you already have human-review files, put them there too.
Start from a **copy** of any folder that holds earlier results: a run overwrites the files it
writes (see [Output files](output-files.html)).

## 3. Run

```r
library(sleepcleanr)
run_pipeline(config = "my_study.yaml", project_dir = "path/to/project",
             include_manual_corrections = TRUE)
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `config` | Path to the config YAML. A relative path is read from `project_dir`, and if it is not there, from the directory you called from. |
| `project_dir` | The project folder. The run changes into it, so every relative path in the YAML (data, manual files) is relative to it. |
| `include_manual_corrections` | **Default `FALSE`.** Whether human-review files are applied. It is an argument of the call, not a YAML setting. See below. |
| `skip_visualization` | `TRUE` skips the figures. |

### The two modes

| | `include_manual_corrections = FALSE` (default) | `= TRUE` |
|---|---|---|
| Human-review files | Treated as absent; the run is algorithmic-only and says so in a banner | Applied, if the files named in the YAML exist |
| Step 5 worksheets | Written | Written |
| Use it for | The first run on new data, to see what the rules flag | Applying the corrections your reviewers have recorded |

The default changed in version 1.4.7. Earlier versions applied the manual files without being asked, so
the same call can give different results before and after.

## 4. What to look for in the console

Each step prints a heading `=== Step N: ... ===`. After a run:

* The last heading tells you how far it got. If the run stops, the error is printed after the last heading.
* Before Step 1 the run prints `=== Rules in effect for this run ===`: every threshold it will use and
  whether it is the default or comes from your config. The same list is saved in `output/effective_rules.csv`.
* Step 5 should print `14. Saving review CSV files with [NEW] prefix...` and a line `verified on disk` for
  each of the two worksheets.
* With manual corrections on you should see `Manual corrections INCLUDED`; with them off, a banner
  `MANUAL CORRECTIONS NOT INCLUDED`.
* Near the end, `[review status]` counts the rows of the error worksheet in each status.

## 5. Where the results are

Working files for the review go to the **project folder** (not `output/`); results go to `output/`.
[Output files](output-files.html) starts with a quick guide to which file and column answers which question (was it changed, does it still need a person, did someone accept it), then lists every file, when it is written and what it is. If something is
missing or an error appears, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.html).

To read a finished run in R without opening files:

```r
res <- pipeline_results()
names(res)
```
